categories.main_business_segments: Public Storage operates primarily in self-storage facility ownership, development, and operation, which is its core business segment. Ancillary operations include tenant reinsurance, merchandise sales (such as locks and boxes), and third-party self-storage management services. The company also holds a significant equity interest in Shurgard Self Storage, which operates in Western Europe. Until July 2022, Public Storage also held an equity interest in PS Business Parks, which was sold during the year.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Public Storage leverages a technology-driven platform for revenue optimization and operational efficiency, including a centralized information network, dynamic pricing, and a robust digital customer experience. Key methods include an industry-leading website, a customer care center, in-store kiosks, and the eRental® digital move-in process. The company also invests in property upgrades, energy efficiency (LED lighting, solar panels), and sustainability initiatives as part of its Property of Tomorrow program.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves both individual and business customers seeking storage solutions, with a focus on personal and small business storage needs. Its primary markets are individuals relocating, downsizing, or needing temporary storage, as well as small businesses requiring inventory or records storage. Public Storage also targets third-party property owners for its management services and offers insurance products to its storage customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Public Storage is the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the United States, with 2,869 facilities across 40 states and a presence in most major metropolitan markets. It also has a 35% equity interest in Shurgard, which operates 266 facilities in seven Western European countries. The company’s U.S. portfolio is especially concentrated in states like California, Texas, Florida, and other major urban centers.
categories.supply_chain_position: Public Storage operates at the downstream end of the real estate supply chain, directly interfacing with end customers through its owned and managed self-storage facilities. It also acts as a service provider to third-party property owners through management contracts and offers ancillary products such as tenant insurance and moving supplies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include maximizing cash flow from existing facilities, expanding through acquisitions and development, and growing ancillary businesses like tenant reinsurance and third-party management. Public Storage invests in technology to enhance the customer experience and operational efficiency, and pursues sustainability initiatives to reduce environmental impact. The company is also focused on brand strength, digital innovation, and selective geographic expansion.
categories.revenue_model: Public Storage generates revenue primarily through rental income from self-storage facilities, which are leased on a month-to-month basis. Additional revenue streams include tenant reinsurance premiums, merchandise sales, and management fees from third-party property management. The company also earns equity income from its investment in Shurgard and previously from PS Business Parks.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Public Storage is the industry leader in the highly fragmented U.S. self-storage market, owning about 9% of total self-storage square footage. Its main competitors include Extra Space Storage, CubeSmart, Life Storage, and regional/local operators. The company’s scale, brand recognition, and technology platform provide significant competitive advantages, enabling higher operating margins and cash flow per square foot compared to smaller operators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, Public Storage had total assets of $17.6 billion and generated $4.18 billion in total revenues for the year. Net income allocable to common shareholders was $4.1 billion, boosted by a $2.1 billion gain from the sale of its PS Business Parks equity investment. The company has demonstrated strong organic growth, with same-store revenue increasing 14.8% in 2022, and has expanded through significant acquisitions and development projects.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Public Storage differentiates itself through its national scale, highly recognized brand, and technology-enabled customer experience, including digital leasing and account management. Its extensive geographic footprint, operational efficiency, and focus on sustainability further enhance its value proposition. The company emphasizes convenience, security, and a seamless digital experience, supported by ongoing investments in property upgrades and customer service.
